\title{Is the Regional Rate Spatially Clustered? Moran's I and Local Clusters on a Synthetic Grid of Regions}

\section{Introduction}

How does the rate vary across the regions in 2023, and are neighbouring regions alike? The study maps the rate, measures spatial autocorrelation with Moran's $I$ and locates local clusters.

\section{Data}

The study covers 30 regions of a synthetic grid with a 2023 rate; the extra-regio code RZZ has no territory and is left out. Table~\ref{tab:rate} describes the rate: its mean is 7.7933 and it ranges from 4.25 to 12.5.

\input{tables/rate.tex}

\section{Results}

Figure~\ref{fig:map_rate} maps the rate. Under queen contiguity Moran's $I$ is 0.5908 against an expectation of $-0.034483$ under no autocorrelation (permutation $p = 0.001$, 999 permutations); with the 4 nearest neighbours as weights it is 0.5832 (Table~\ref{tab:moran}). Neighbouring regions are alike under both definitions.

\input{tables/moran.tex}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.8\textwidth]{fig_map_rate.pdf}
\caption{The 2023 rate in five quantile classes (synthetic regions).}
\label{fig:map_rate}
\end{figure}

The local indicators find 7 high-high and 4 low-low regions at the 5\% level (Figure~\ref{fig:map_lisa}); with 30 local tests about 1.5 would be significant by chance.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.8\textwidth]{fig_map_lisa.pdf}
\caption{LISA clusters under queen contiguity, $p < 0.05$ (synthetic regions).}
\label{fig:map_lisa}
\end{figure}

\section{Conclusion}

The rate is spatially clustered on this synthetic grid: high values in the north-east, low values in the south-west, under either neighbour definition. The grid is synthetic, and Moran's $I$ describes association between neighbours, not its cause.
